CableConnected logs are only for resolving CableDisconnected errors.
I don't think we should add this for an entire section like this.  Can you add it as NOLINTNEXTLINE in multiple places where needed instead?
Thank you for the suggestion. I’ve updated it to use NOLINTNEXTLINE in the specific places instead.
Done.  In the future, please mark the comment as resolved on your own when you've taken care of it.

Why is this a warning?  Or even a message at all?  We already committed an event for it; I don't think we also need a log.  But "CableConnected" seems like a good thing, not a warning.  Shouldn't it be "info"?
Appreciate your review. I kept the warning level as it was before, but I’ve changed it to debug level now.
Done
You only need to resolve the CableDisconnected when Cable gets connected on that port. There is no resolution for CableConnected.
Thanks for pointing it out. I misunderstood the resolved field in the log entry and thought it was an invalid flag in a positive log.

What do you mean by "CableConnected log that was not emitted"?

At the beginning we don't send CableConnected logs if the cable are already connected. They are only sent in response to resolution for CableDisconnected errors.

I think I misunderstood the design of cable-monitor, since our ventura-phosphor-multi-gpio-monitor.json recorded positive events instead of negative ones.
So I wondered why this did not emit a positive event log, which is why I submitted this PR.

Is it possible that we try to `generateCableEvent` for the same `type` twice in a row?  I guess that's probably not possible right now, but the way the code is currently written we could end up resolving a `disconnected` event while also trying to create a new one.

I think the GPIO controller must detect the level change and then trigger an IRQ to inform the BMC of the edge event.
I guess you just mentioned the bouncing case. This could happen when the cable has a poor connection. If there’s a double trigger in a short period, we should check the cable.

Connected is a positive acknowledgement and an event (not error), so you don't need to resolve it.

Disconnected is an error which will be resolved by Connected event.

Thats the reason we don't mark the connected as Pending. The current implemented logic is correct based on the event definition in https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/State/Cable.events.yaml

Thanks for the detailed explanation. I now understand CableConnected logs are only for resolving CableDisconnected errors. If there’s no need to log positive events in the future (like we did with gpio-monitor on Ventura), then this PR should be abandoned.
